newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan PM tells Israel to remove peace obstacles.
newsitem.headline: Jordan PM tells Israel to remove peace obstacles.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti urged Israel on Monday to remove obstacles in peace talks with the Palestinians, the state news agency Petra said.

It said Kabariti reiterated support for the Palestinians in their peace negotiations with Israel and called for Israel to "remove all hurdles and difficulties facing progress in Palestinian-Israeli talks."
Kabariti made the comments during a meeting with Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat, who Petra said arrived with a letter for King Hussein on the crisis from PLO leader Yasser Arafat.
Erekat was quoted as saying "Jordan stands with us in the same trench in facing the latest Israeli moves and in providing us with all the support and help at all levels."

Petra said Arafat's letter concerned the deepening crisis in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks, including the outcome of a meeting on Sunday between chief Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas, known as Abu Mazen, and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy.

Abbas, an architect of the groundbreaking 1993 Israel-PLO peace accord, subsequently submitted his resignation in protest over Israel's decision to hand over nine percent of rural areas of the West Bank instead of the 30 percent Palestinians demanded.
Kabariti emphasised "the need to respect all the signed accords between the Palestinian and Israeli sides, especially those relating to redeployment of the Israeli army in the West Bank."
The Palestinians are furious that Israel unilaterally set the extent of the withdrawal, the first of three under a 1995 Israeli-Palestinian deal and reaffirmed in a January accord.
Kabariti also attacked plans for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, which has outraged many Jordanians. Jordan has a large Palestinian population.
Amman agrees with the Palestinians that Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem prejudices negotiations on the city in final peace talks due to start on March 17.
"There should be no tampering with the status quo on the grounds that this would jeopardise the final status negotiations," Kabariti said.
